---
applyTo: "src/coordinator/**,src/runner/**,src/gridtest/**,tests/coordinator/**,tests/runner/**,tests/sample/**,scripts/**"

# Grid backend (coordinator, runner, framework)

- **One wire contract, three consumers.** The coordinator (`src/coordinator/coordinator.py`, `schemas.py`), the runner (`src/runner/runner_client.py`) and Amplify (`src/amplify_server/grid_data.py`, `consolidated.py`, `routes/grid.py`, `static/js/grid.js`, `dashboard.js`) share endpoints and JSON fields (`/api/runner/lease`, `/api/runners/{id}/heartbeat`, `/api/runners/{id}/exit`, `runner_id`, `assigned_runner`). Change one side and you change all three, with their tests and the docs, in the same change. New capabilities are announced in `FEATURES` (`src/coordinator/config.py`) so Amplify can tell when a coordinator is too old.
- **The database is migrated by hand.** `Base.metadata.create_all()` never alters an existing table. Add a column with an idempotent statement in `_MIGRATIONS` (`src/coordinator/db.py`); do a rename like `migrate_worker_to_runner` does, in a function that runs before `create_all()`, is safe to repeat, and has a test against a legacy-shaped database (`tests/coordinator/test_schema_migration.py`). Renames are one-way: say so in the docs.
- **Leasing SQL is PostgreSQL-only** (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`). The SQLite-backed tests cannot prove it, so after touching `leasing.py` or `services.py` run `pytest tests/coordinator/test_lease_db.py` with `GRID_TEST_DATABASE_URL` set to a scratch database.
- **Two tokens, on purpose.** `API_TOKEN` / `GRID_API_TOKEN` is the full token (Amplify, the seeder). `POD_API_TOKEN` is what runners hold and opens only what a pod needs; everything else answers 403 (enforced in `src/coordinator/schemas.py`). Test code runs inside the runner pods and can read what the pod holds, so a pod must never get the full token, the per-chunk lease token goes only on result submit and Allure upload, and the runner strips `GRID_API_TOKEN` from the pytest process. Compare tokens in constant time. Do not weaken `tests/coordinator/test_pod_token.py` or `tests/runner/test_lease_token_secrecy.py`.
- **Report environments are generated JavaScript.** `src/coordinator/report_environments.py` writes the Allure config (one environment per `browser` label) that the CLI executes, and the label values come from files a pod's test code can write. Only a valid environment id (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`) may be pasted in; everything else goes in as escaped JSON; never name the file `allurerc.*` (the CLI loads it from its working directory unasked). Allure 3.16.0 has no `dynamicEnvironments`, so keep the explicit list.
- **Cancelling a run** (`POST /api/runs/{id}/cancel`, full token only; Amplify's `POST /api/grid/runs/<id>/cancel` limits it to the run's owner or an admin) turns its pending and running chunks into `cancelled`. A runner whose chunk was cancelled gets **403** on result submit, and that must stay a 403 checked before the lease-token check: the runner drops the results and carries on, while any other status makes it retry and then exit, and a chunk without a token would otherwise accept the write.
- **Live view** (`src/coordinator/live_view.py`, `src/runner/live_view.py`, `src/amplify_server/routes/grid_live.py`). A pod registers its VNC password with the pod token; the coordinator stores the address the request came **from** and the fixed port 5900, and only the full token reads them back. Never accept a host or port from a pod or a browser: test code holds the pod token, and Amplify connects wherever the record points. Amplify re-checks owner-or-admin on both the `view` call and the WebSocket, and the WebSocket refuses foreign origins because it authenticates with the session cookie. A failing display or VNC server must only turn live view off, never fail a chunk.
- **Extra pytest arguments** (`src/amplify_server/grid_args.py` → `src/coordinator/pytest_args.py` → `src/runner/pytest_args.py`) travel as `[{"flag", "style", "value"}]`, never as a command string, and the runner forms the words and puts them before the `--` that precedes the test ids. The three modules apply the same rules and reserved options (`tests/amplify_server/grid/test_grid_pytest_args.py` compares them): change all three together. Never let one through that the runner sets itself (`-p`, `-n`, `--alluredir`, `-o`, ...).
- **Archive limits are shared.** The caps on code snapshots (member count, sizes) are deliberately the same in `src/amplify_server/grid_snapshot.py`, `src/coordinator/tar_limits.py` and `src/runner/tar_guard.py`. Change them together; `tests/amplify_server/grid/test_grid_volume.py` pins the member cap.
- **Runner image layout** (`Dockerfile.grid-runner`): `/app` is root-owned and not writable by the runtime uid, because test code runs as that uid. A new module that `runner_client.py` imports must be added to the Dockerfile's `COPY` line and to `Dockerfile.grid-runner.dockerignore`; `tests/runner/test_image_layout.py` checks both. The coordinator image copies `src/coordinator/*.py`, so a new coordinator module goes at the top level of `src/coordinator/`. Each image has its own pinned dependency file at the repo root: `amplify-requirements.txt`, `coordinator-requirements.txt`, `runner-requirements.txt`. The runner image is the complete test setup (browser plus every package the test repos import); a repo's own `requirements.txt` is never installed on the pods, so a package a test repo needs is added, pinned, to `runner-requirements.txt`.
- **Tests run on Python 3.12**, like the images. `tests/runner/` and `tests/coordinator/` are plain pytest folders with their own `conftest.py`; `tests/sample/` holds the Playwright sample suite that is baked into the runner image and needs a browser.
- Vocabulary: "runner", never "worker" (see `.github/copilot-instructions.md`).
